f01.title: A shared record for the laboratory.
f01.copy: LIMS means Laboratory Information Management System. It helps the team know which sample they have, what work is needed, who is doing it, and which results have been checked.
f01.why: People and equipment do the physical laboratory work. LIMS connects its records, responsibilities and history.
f01.subtitle: Start here · no account needed
f01.lead: LIMS means Laboratory Information Management System. It connects the sample, the work people do and the results they report.
f01.panelTitle: Imagine a labelled bag of soil arrives.
f01.question: A sample is “expected”. Has its container arrived?
f01.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Expected means it is planned or registered; the lab confirms physical arrival separately.
f01.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. Expected means it is planned or registered; the lab confirms physical arrival separately.

f02.title: One sample. Connected work.
f02.copy: A sample can need several tests. Its sample page, assigned tasks and report are connected views of the same work, not separate copies to enter again.
f02.why: A project can involve several laboratories. Your account controls which records you can see; the sample identity follows the work.
f02.subtitle: The same sample throughout
f02.lead: One sample can require pH, texture and other analyses.
f02.panelTitle: One bag of soil. Several tests.
f02.question: One sample needs pH and texture tests. How many sample records is that?
f02.feedbackCorrect: Correct. One sample record can have several analyses, assigned tasks and results.
f02.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. One sample record can have several analyses, assigned tasks and results.

f03.title: Where should I go next?
f03.copy: Home shows what needs attention. Samples tells you the story of a sample. The workbench is where a technician records the assigned work.
f03.why: A saved draft is still work in progress. Submitting it is a separate handover to the person who checks it.
f03.subtitle: Your map of the platform
f03.lead: These destinations show different parts of connected work.
f03.panelTitle: Start with the task in front of you.
f03.question: You saved a draft result. Who acts next?
f03.optCompleteSubmit: I still need to complete and submit it
f03.optReviewerApprove: The reviewer can already approve it
f03.feedbackCorrect: Correct. A draft is still yours to complete; submission is the handover for review.
f03.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. A draft is still yours to complete; submission is the handover for review.

welcome.name: Welcome
welcome.title: Your first day, made clear.
welcome.copy: Follow a sample from arrival to its final report. Choose a quick overview, the full lab story, or the work your role handles.
welcome.why: A useful introduction connects each action to its purpose. You can pause, skip and return whenever you need.

identity.name: Your role
identity.title: Start with the right role.
identity.copy: Your account determines which laboratory and tasks you can access. The story changes roles; your real account changes only when you sign in.
identity.why: A reception officer, technician and reviewer have different responsibilities. A tutorial must never bypass those permissions.

field.name: Field to lab
field.title: Expected is not received.
field.copy: Field records bring identity and location into the project. Five samples may be expected, but arrival must still be checked at the laboratory.
field.why: Kobo provenance helps connect a physical container to its field record. A successful import does not confirm physical custody.

intake.name: Reception
intake.title: Match the container first.
intake.copy: Check the field ID, project and location. Record the mass and condition only after the container is physically present.
intake.why: The laboratory sample ID is the working label. Preserving its field identity makes later results traceable.

prepare.name: Preparation
prepare.title: Preparation is evidence.
prepare.copy: Practice the checklist below. In the real lab, confirm a step only when you have carried it out and have the required record.
prepare.why: Drying and preparation are procedural steps. A numerical placeholder cannot establish that material is ready for analysis.

bench.name: Analysis bench
bench.title: One method. A clear batch.
bench.copy: Use a method worksheet to work through samples consistently. Read the identity, method and unit before entering a result.
bench.why: A draft, a recorded determination and a submitted result are different states. Submission is the handover to the reviewer.

texture.name: Texture
texture.title: Three fractions. One result.
texture.copy: Sand, silt and clay belong together. Try a total that does not close, then correct it before marking the practice complete.
texture.why: The real method controls precision and tolerance. Texture class is a derived, validated result; this preview does not invent a classification.

spectra.name: Spectroscopy
spectra.title: The evidence is the spectrum.
spectra.copy: Inspect a curve, its axes and the sample link. MIR and NIR need spectral evidence, rather than a single number labelled reflectance.
spectra.why: Import, spectral quality checks, predictions and approved library records are separate stages. A plotted curve alone is not an accepted result.

review.name: Review
review.title: Review the evidence.
review.copy: A manager reviews submitted work. Practice returning one result with a clear reason so the technician knows what needs attention.
review.why: Unsubmitted work is not ready for review. Acceptance of an item and final release of a sample or report are separate decisions.

trace.name: Map & report
trace.title: A result with a history.
trace.copy: The map explains dependencies and handovers. The report connects the final result to its method, version and review history.
trace.why: A workflow map must reflect recorded events. A tutorial must never draw a completed state over an incomplete real sample.

resources.name: Lab & data
resources.title: The lab is connected.
resources.copy: Check equipment readiness and inventory lots. Follow field provenance from Kobo and learn how authorized results can be exchanged with SIS.
resources.why: Viewing stock does not consume it, and previewing an export does not prove it was delivered. Each action has its own record.

finish.name: Your next step
finish.title: Ready to explore your role.
finish.copy: You have seen how the work fits together. Next, use the account and designated test samples agreed with the facilitator.
finish.why: A tutorial is an introduction, not a competency certificate or proof that every application workflow has passed acceptance.

intake.title: Physical arrival
intake.initialStatus: Match the label and enter a positive mass.
intake.success: Practice checked: the container matches and a positive mass is recorded in this exercise.
intake.error: Check the container identity and enter a positive mass. A mismatch needs resolution.

prep.title: Preparation practice
prep.check0: Match the sample label to its intake record.
prep.check1: Verify the applicable drying and preparation records.
prep.check2: Confirm prepared portions are labelled for their analyses.
prep.verifiedStatus: Practice checklist verified. No actual preparation record was changed.

bench.initialStatus: This field belongs to the preview, not the real workbench.
bench.previewSuffix: In LIMS, confirm the configured method and limits before recording.

texture.statusOk: Practice values close correctly. The real method defines precision and tolerance.
texture.statusError: Use 0–100% for each fraction and make this practice total equal 100%.
texture.classDesc: The production report should use the validated classification rule and result revision. This guide does not calculate a substitute class.

spectra.title: Spectral file practice
spectra.ariaSvg: Illustrative MIR curve, wavenumber descending from 4000 to 400 inverse centimetres
spectra.svgLabel: Illustrative relative signal · synthetic, not an instrument export
spectra.note: A source spectrum contains a sequence of measurements across a spectral axis.
spectra.ribbon: A raw scan, a quality-checked spectrum and an approved prediction are different records.

review.qcNote: QC evidence: needs inspection, not assumed PASS.
review.title: Return for correction
review.label: Tell the technician what to check
review.placeholder: For example: verify the replicate discrepancy
review.initialStatus: A meaningful reason is required before returning a result.

res.equipmentDesc: Check operational status and calibration before use. Viewing an asset does not book or calibrate it.
res.inventoryDesc: Check quantity, expiry, status and storage location. An inventory view is not a stock consumption record.
res.koboDesc: Look for source form, field identifier and location provenance. Configured connectivity does not prove a successful import or receipt.
res.sisDesc: Review the allowed dataset and its metadata. A payload preview does not prove delivery or acknowledgement by a national SIS.
res.langDesc: The implementation follows the platform's five language options.

glossary.lims: Laboratory Information Management System: connected records for laboratory work.
glossary.sample: The physical material and its digital record.
glossary.project: A group of related samples and work; it can involve several labs.
glossary.spectrum: A measured signal across a range, saved as data rather than one number.
glossary.qc: Quality control: checks on the evidence and its suitability.
glossary.sis: Soil Information System: a connection for authorized soil information exchange.
glossary.lot: A particular batch of laboratory material.
glossary.workbench: The technician's place to record assigned work.
glossary.draft: Saved work that is not yet submitted for checking.
glossary.submit: Hand completed work to the person who checks it.
glossary.auditHistory: A record of who did what and when.
